title: SM washout and epoch alignment - experiment notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an ad-hoc investigation into an intermittent GPU utilization pattern we've been calling 'SM washout' — periods after CUDA-graph replay where a subset of SMs appears lightly utilized for tens to hundreds of milliseconds despite kernels still running. Goal is to record hypotheses, measurement recipes, small reproducer traces, observed correlations with microbatching/aperture, and concrete follow-ups.

Background / why this matters:
- Seen as a contributor to 99.9th percentile token latency spikes on heavy-stream workloads (chat-like decoder).
- Not fully explained by host-side queueing; Nsight traces show active kernels but uneven SM occupancy heatmaps.
- Suspected interactions: CUDA graph rebind, L2 eviction/warmer delays, persistent kernel launch ramp, and clock gating (SM clocks going to lower P-states transiently).

Quick summary of findings (high level):
- Replaying CUDA graphs after an idle gap often results in an initial epoch (~30-120ms) of ~30–60% effective SM utilization despite 100% nominal active warps reported by nvtx markers.
- Microbatch aperture (how many tokens are prefetched into KV cache before decode kernels spawn) affects washout magnitude: smaller apertures => longer washout.
- Forcible warmup (a short synthetic workload that touches all warps/blocks) reduces washout and eliminates the tail for that session.
- Power/clock state transitions (observed via nvidia-smi sampling) align with some washouts; on multi-tenant nodes this is noisy but reproducible on dedicated instance.

Repro recipe (minimal):
1) Model: small decoder-only 3B-ish transformer (repro harness lives in serving-runtime/tools/repro/sm-washout).
2) Config: microbatch size 1, beam 1, kv-prefetch off, cuda-graph capture/replay enabled, persistent kernel enabled.
3) Host command to run (example):
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./repro_decode --config=aperture_small --capture-mode=graph --replays=1000 --nvtx
4) Nsight session:
   nsys profile --output=trace_smwash --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --sample-freq=1000 ./repro_decode --config=aperture_small --capture-mode=graph
5) Collect: trace file, nvidia-smi log (nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 100), and CUPTI kernel occupancy counters (via CUPTI helper in repro harness).

Key trace observations (from 2026-04-12 run on A100-sxm):
- Timeline: graph replay start at t=0, first decode kernel launches between 1–3ms, but SM occupancy heatmaps show many SMs in the 20–40% bucket for first 70ms. Occupancy metrics from CUPTI show high resident warps but low active warps in a subset of SMs.
- NVTX markers: host-side NVTX indicates 'decode-step' active during washout; wall-clock of host is continuous (no host-side starvation).
- Kernel-level timelines: many small kernels (attention heads) serialized in a fashion that causes some SMs to be idle while others are saturated — evidence of poor warp distribution across blocks for the current kernel-grid mapping.
- L2 traffic: increased read-after-eviction misses in the first epoch; suggests cold L2/KV warmup.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Persistent kernel scheduler warm-up: CUDA graph rebind triggers scheduler to place threads differently for the first few launches -> suboptimal SM spreading.
2) KV/L2 cold start: large KV lookups populate L2 asynchronously, some SMs stall waiting for memory lines.
3) Power/clock gating: SMs downclocked immediately after idle; clocks take tens of ms to ramp back once kernels fire.
4) Kernel launch pacing combined with microbatch boundaries leads to transient serialization which shows up as washout.

Tests run and short results:
- Forced-warmup test: insert 100 us synthetic all-SM touch before graph replay. Result: washout amplitude dropped by ~80% and 99.9th latency improved ~18%.
- Prefetch-on test: enable KV prefetch (populate hot cache) for next N tokens. Result: washout amplitude reduced but not eliminated; L2 miss rate lower.
- No-graph fallback: run without CUDA graph capture (direct launches). Result: washout almost gone but average kernel launch overhead increases latency by ~5% — tradeoff.
- Clock-lock test: set persistent max clocks via nvidia-smi to prevent DVFS. Result: washout reduced significantly on dedicated instance; can't rely on this in shared environments.

Measurement recipes and command snippets (keeps reproducible):
- nsys: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=trace_smwash --wait=ms --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none ./repro_decode --run-id=smwash
- nvidia-smi polling: while true; do date +%s.%3N, nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,clocks.sm,power.draw --format=csv,noheader,nounits; sleep 0.01; done > nvsmi-smwash.csv
- CUPTI helper (in repro tool): repro_decode --cuptri-counters=active_warps,issued_ipc,sm_efficiency --cuptri-sample-interval=10ms

Open datapoints to collect next: (short-term backlog)
- Per-SM occupancy time series (CUPTI or low-overhead sampling) to confirm if same SMs are repeatedly underutilized.
- Repeat tests across different driver versions (510 vs 535) and kernel release to detect driver scheduler changes.
- Test on different GPU families (A100 vs H100) — initial H100 run shows smaller washout but still present.
- Vary microbatch aperture continuously and measure washout vs. throughput tradeoff.

Mitigations to experiment with (cheap -> intrusive):
- Cheap: Add a 50–200us all-SM warmup before first graph replay. Pros: tiny cost, easy to roll to prod; Cons: overhead on every session start.
- Medium: Adaptive prefetch that triggers only after cold-start or when graph replay detected. Pros: targeted; Cons: more complex heuristics.
- Heavy: Avoid CUDA-graph capture for tail-sensitive routes, or instrument driver-level flags to prefer direct launch for first N steps. Cons: increased per-token CPU overhead.

Engineering action items (owners):
- Samir: Add warmup patch to repro harness and run 24-hour soak across Dedicated pool (due 2026-04-20).
- Lina: Add per-SM CUPTI sampling in telemetry and bake into console heatmap (prototype by 2026-04-25).
- Riley: Run driver matrix tests and file kernel-driver regression tickets if results differ (due 2026-04-22).
- Hiro: Prototype adaptive prefetch heuristic and test in staging (POC by 2026-05-01).

Notes / stray observations:
- When other tenants on the node experienced high memcpy traffic (NVLink/PCIe bursts), washout magnitude grew – points to memory subsystem interference.
- Some traces show a 'ripple' pattern where SMs recover in groups of 4–8 SMs — suggests scheduler favors certain SM blocks during initial ramp.
- Nsight screenshot references: trace_smwash_nsight_20260412_page3.png (stored in shared drive under /misc/profiles).

Questions for discussion at next sync:
- Do we accept a small warmup tax for latency sensitive routes? Which percentiles/users?
- Can runtime detect a graph-replay cold start cheaply (host-side signal) without CUPTI?
- Is there a safe default for cloud multi-tenant nodes (e.g., minimal warmup) vs dedicated nodes?

Appendix: quick grep-able tags and files used locally:
- repro harness: serving-runtime/tools/repro/sm-washout
- nsight traces: /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/profiles/trace_smwash_2026-04-12.nsys-rep
- nvidia-smi logs: /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/profiles/nvsmi-smwash-2026-04-12.csv
- quick diff: git rev-parse HEAD -> feature/sm-washout-2026-04-12 (PR linked above)

If we converge on warmup as default mitigation, we should quantify total cost across workloads and add a configurable flag in runtime config (warmup.duration_us, warmup.enabled)
